justification.completionRateSource: NOT A THRESHOLD — the field the other three bars are computed from, and the reasoning for it is this block's $comment at length: profile.pump_tokens[].complete agreed with our tape 67/67 on the completion flag with no in-window launch missing, while every published aggregate is a trailing ~7.5-day window their own alert text calls 'lifetime', and /deployer-hunter/{wallet}/tokens is bonded-only and so has no denominator at all. justification.minTokens: MadeOnSol's own spec tells consumers to gate on labeled_tokens >= 3. That is far too low: on our subject deployer a 22-token window read 0.6818 against a true 0.4310, so a window of ~22 was enough to be wrong by 58% relative. 25 is the floor at which their sliding-window artefact stops being the whole measurement, and it is 8x their published gate. NAME THE POPULATION, THOUGH: that evidence is about the VENDOR'S TRAILING WINDOW, while rank.mjs compares `completion.tokens` of whatever history reading the run produced — by default the creation-derived merged listing, which is larger and therefore easier to clear than the window this figure was measured on. The bar is a 'worth scoring at all' filter rather than a claim about the deployer, so the mismatch is bounded, but the two are not the same count and no measurement fixes 25 against the merged one. It is NOT enough for a lifetime claim, which is why the span is reported alongside and why long-horizon consistency is reported UNMEASURED.
justification.minCompletionRate: 0.25, HELD BY CAPTAIN DECISION 231a (2026-08-04), WHICH MOVES NO VALUE AND REWRITES THIS ENTRY: the defect was that the earlier text named NO READING, which made the number unauditable — a completion rate is not one quantity here and the two the tool computes differ by an order of magnitude on the same wallets. NAME THE READING FIRST. This bar is compared against the CREATION-DERIVED MERGED HISTORY that screen.mjs gates on by default — which mints the wallet CREATED, `historySource: "creation-derived"`, the default since record schema 4 with --ownership-only as the opt-out, and the reading of every candidate in the last real run (`runs/2026-08-04.json`, schema 12, 82 candidates, 82 of 82 creation-derived). That reading's median window on those candidates is 147.1 days and its median token count 1,386, and it is the WHOLE creation history for 57 of the 82 (`creation.wholeHistory`). THE VENDOR 70-RECORD PAGE IS A DIFFERENT AND SHORTER QUANTITY AND THIS BAR IS NOT MEASURED ON IT: median span 3.4 days on the same 82 wallets, page-capped at 70 records on 63 of them, and SUCCESS-BIASED rather than merely short, because ownership is a sellable position and the ones worth handing on are the winners — `yHCxHBEa…` shows 280 of the 749 mints it created and so reads 1.0000 on the page against 0.3071 on the gate reading. --ownership-only runs and feed.mjs read that page (FEED.md, 'Why the gate here reads ownership'), so the feed ledger's `completionRate` is not this quantity and a bar argued on one does not transfer to the other. WHAT FIXES THE VALUE, in order of weight. (1) THE CONTROL IS A HARD CEILING. `7ufmve7Z…` — the known-competent operator Stage 0 requires this gate to PASS — reads 0.4325 (109 of 252) on the gate reading, so ANY BAR ABOVE 0.4325 EXCLUDES A WALLET WE KNOW IS GOOD; and its own month-to-month rates span 0.256 (0.381, 0.354, 0.610, 0.375, 0.548, 0.429), so anything above ~0.35 puts it within one ordinary month of exclusion. Its committed-tape lifetime rate, 0.4310 over 239 launches and 103 bonded, is the same ceiling read off this repo's own primary record. (2) WHAT THE BAR DOES ON THE SCREEN'S OWN POPULATION, re-derivable offline from the committed record: over the 66 of that run's 82 candidates that clear minTokens and minSpanDays the median rate is 0.0187, 4 clear 0.25, only 2 clear 0.35, and 0.60 admits NOBODY — a bar that empties the run has spent the keyed allowance to produce no Stage 2 population at all. (3) A RATE BAR CANNOT SEPARATE SKILL FROM THE REGIME ARTEFACT, BECAUSE THE ARTEFACT READS HIGHER. The two wallets whose rates are a post-break short-window artefact read 1.0000 (`yHCxHBEa…`, old-regime record 0.1369) and 0.9429 (`GeBJSHK4…`, old-regime record 0.0462) while the control reads 0.5429 on the same vendor page and 0.4325 on the gate reading. There is no bar that removes those two and keeps the control: RAISING THIS NUMBER REMOVES THE OPERATOR AND KEEPS THE ARTEFACTS. What distinguishes them is window length and reading, not rate, so the instrument for them is an evidence-window rule or the reading itself — not this bar. (4) THE ASYMMETRY THAT DECIDES WHERE IN THE 0.25–0.35 BAND TO SIT, and it points DOWN. A false REJECTION here is permanent and invisible: the wallet is graded, filed in feed/ledger.json and never offered again (ledger.mjs; the feed never re-polls a wallet already graded). A false ACCEPTANCE is visible and cheap: it costs Stage 2 keyless requests and is then refused by stage2_entry.minRoomLeft — which is exactly what Stage 0 demonstrates on every run, passing `7ufmve7Z…` on this gate and refusing it on room. This gate is 'necessary and nowhere near sufficient' (this block's $comment), so it is deliberately set to fail towards acceptance. 0.25 is also MadeOnSol's own published 'good'-tier bar, which is where the number came from; it is not what holds it now. PROVENANCE, AND IT IS SPLIT BECAUSE THE TWO HALVES ARE AUDITED DIFFERENTLY. FROM THE COMMITTED `runs/2026-08-04.json`, re-derivable offline with no vendor call: the 82-candidate figures (82 of 82 creation-derived, median gate-reading window 147.1 days, median 1,386 tokens, whole creation history on 57 of 82, vendor median span 3.4 days, vendor page capped at 70 records on 63 of 82), the 66-candidate sweep (median 0.0187, 4 clear 0.25, 2 clear 0.35, none clears 0.60), and `yHCxHBEa…`'s page-against-gate pair (1.0000 on the vendor page against 0.3071 on the gate reading, 280 of the 749 mints its ownership listing shows). FROM `slot-zero-gate-bar-measure-own-population` (held in firstmate's records, not in this repo), because these do NOT reproduce from that run record: the control `7ufmve7Z…`'s 0.4325 gate reading, its 0.5429 vendor-page reading and its 0.256 month-to-month range are §6; `GeBJSHK4…`'s 0.9429 is §4.2's live re-read of 2026-08-05, and its §0 summary quotes the same figure; the old-regime records 0.1369 (`yHCxHBEa…`) and 0.0462 (`GeBJSHK4…`) are §0 and §4.2; and the argument itself — the ceiling, the sweep's reading, the artefact comparison and the asymmetry — is §6, §6b, §7 and §8. AND THE VENDOR 70-RECORD PAGE SLIDES, so two snapshots of one wallet days apart legitimately differ and neither is stale: `GeBJSHK4…` reads 0.9429 on that 2026-08-05 re-read and 0.957143 in this repo's own committed `runs/2026-07-29-elite.json` and `feed/ledger.json`, one launch apart on a 70-record window — that gap is a property of the surface, and it is itself part of why this bar is measured on the creation-derived reading rather than on the page. That report's §8 recommends the 0.25–0.35 band and does not choose within it; 231a chooses 0.25 and changes nothing about what the screen admits. ONE CORRECTION TO IT MADE HERE RATHER THAN INHERITED: it dates the creation-derived default to 'schema 12', which is the SCHEMA OF THE RUN IT MEASURED — the default arrived at record schema 4.
justification.minSpanDays: A high rate earned inside a single day is a burst, not a record — and this bar measures exactly that: rank.mjs compares `completion.spanDays`, which is FIRST DEPLOY TO LAST DEPLOY over the gate's history reading, not time-to-bond. The two are not the same quantity and an earlier version of this entry justified the first with a distribution of the second, computed from `curve_last_tx_s`; that column is formally ruled a valid upper BOUND and not a usable timing (data/population-tape-2026-07-29/IMPORT.md, Corrections 4, median overshoot 8.85x), so the clause is withdrawn rather than re-derived and the column is not quoted here. The measured median graduation time on this operator is 1,042 s = 17.4 MINUTES (IMPORT.md, Corrections 5), so 14 days is orders of magnitude above what a launch needs to resolve: this bar exists to refuse a wallet whose whole history is one burst, not to wait for bonding. NOTE THE RESIDUAL GAP, which no span bar closes: a wallet that deploys most of its tokens in the last 48 hours of a 14-day span still clears this, and its unresolved launches then depress its completion rate — which errs towards rejection, the direction this tool prefers to fail in.

The floor is deliberately below the cap so that a dropped launch costs a launch rather than the whole candidate's verdict; see maxLaunchesPerCandidate for what the gap absorbs. An earlier version of this entry cited that bucket as the anchor for 8 and misquoted it as 22 — 22 is the era's launch count in the same report's three-era split table, which states no quartiles at all. The reader's recourse is in the record: every run record carries entry.launchesSampled, so what a verdict was computed over is visible rather than assumed.
